newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria sacks top police officers.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria sacks top police officers.

text.p: The Nigerian police has retired three senior officers in a sweeping reorganisation of the police force, state radio reported on Friday.

The three deputy inspectors-generals retired included Archibong Nkana, the top detective who headed investigations into the murder in June of the senior wife of Moshood Abiola, widely believed to have won 1993 presidential elections.
Abiola has been in detention since June 1994 when he proclaimed himself president in defiance of the military government.
State radio said the retirements were part of the restructuring approved after a probe of the police force.
The police recently announced the dismissal nationwide of more than 500 policemen.
A police statement on Thursday said the police force had been split into five departments with each headed by an assistant inspector-general.

The Nigerian police has been under public criticism for failing to find the killers of several high profile persons, the latest being Kudirat Abiola, who was sprayed with bullets in her car along a Lagos road.
Police investigation has made no breakthrough so far and the police this week blamed lack of information from the public to help find the woman's killers.
Kudirat Abiola had been campaigning for the release of her husband.
